claude_only.name: Which named time scale does this temporal value use, and is that scale explicitly declared or merely assumed?
Which body defines and publishes this scale, and through which serial publication is its realisation disseminated?
Is the scale continuous, or may it contain inserted or removed seconds that break naive arithmetic?
What is the offset from this scale to UTC at a given instant, and from when is that offset valid?
Which scale is used for the underlying storage representation, and does it differ from the scale used for display or comparison?
Which body decides a leap adjustment, and by which dated instrument was the most recent decision announced?
What is the cumulative TAI-UTC value at a given instant, and when does the consulted leap table expire?
How does this system represent or avoid the 60th second, and is that behaviour declared?
What happens to stored durations and orderings computed before a leap adjustment took effect?
How will the planned change to the UT1-UTC tolerance by 2035 affect assumptions currently baked into this Dimension?
Is the leap table currently in use still valid, and what is done when it has expired?
Does every recorded instant carry an explicit offset or Z, and are unqualified local times rejected at the boundary?
Is the offset a known local offset, an assertion of UTC preference, or a declaration that the local offset is unknown?
What fractional-second precision is stored, and is stored precision distinguished from measured precision?
Are event time and observation or ingestion time recorded separately for this record class?
When an instant is annotated with a time zone, is that annotation critical, and what must happen if it contradicts the offset?
Which identifier scheme is this zone identifier drawn from, and is the value canonical or an alias?
Which stable identifier does this Dimension persist when the upstream registry renames or relinks a zone?
Are zone abbreviations, numeric offsets or country codes ever used to identify a zone in this system?
What happens to stored references when a zone is split, merged or retired upstream?
Which geographic region does this identifier actually cover, and is that coverage authoritative for jurisdictional purposes?
What is the complete ordered series of offset transitions for this zone over the period the data must serve?
Until what instant is the zone data explicitly valid, and how is behaviour beyond that point derived?
Was a given transition a historical fact, a scheduled future change, or a prediction from a repeating rule?
Which upstream release supplied this transition series, and has any transition changed between releases?
Is the recorded pre-1970 history evidence-backed or reconstructed, and is that distinction visible to consumers?
Which projection formats must this transition series be emitted in, and are they lossless with respect to each other?
When a stated local time falls in a transition gap, is it rejected, shifted forward, or shifted by the gap duration?
When a stated local time is ambiguous, is the earlier or later occurrence chosen, and can the caller override?
If the supplied offset contradicts the supplied zone identifier, which wins, and is the annotation critical?
Is the resolved offset persisted alongside the local time so the resolution is reproducible later?
How are recurring local-time series handled when a future instance lands in a gap created by a later rule change?
Which authority is legally competent to change standard time or daylight arrangements for this territory?
By which dated instrument was the current arrangement established, and where was it officially published?
What is the procedure and evidentiary threshold for changing a boundary or an exemption?
When does the change take legal effect, and how much notice was given before that instant?
Who owns the record of this arrangement in the adopting Dimension, and who mirrors it into machine data?
Is the machine data currently consistent with the legal instrument, and what is done while they diverge?
Which registered calendar key identifies this system, and is that key current or deprecated in favour of another?
Is the system solar, lunar or lunisolar, and does it use intercalary days, intercalary months or both?
Where two keys describe the same tradition but differ in determination method, which one governs this record?
How are leap months represented and ordered when a date or recurrence falls in one?
Which calendar is assumed when none is declared, and is that assumption territory-dependent?
Can this calendar's dates be converted losslessly to and from the proleptic Gregorian representation used for storage?
Which era does a given date fall in, and how is the era boundary expressed unambiguously?
What identifies the era stably — the mnemonic code or the numeric type used for name lookup?
Does this calendar inherit eras from another calendar, and does that inheritance affect ordering?
What process adds a new era, and what is the lead time between proclamation and effect?
Are year numbers within the era counted forward only, and how are dates before the calendar's epoch expressed?
Which territory's week data governs this computation, and how was that territory determined?
What are the first day of week, the minimum days in the first week and the weekend days for that territory?
Does week numbering follow the ISO week-date rules or the territory's own rules, and is that choice declared?
Is the week-start used in recurrence expansion the same as the locale week-start, and what happens if they differ?
How is a weekend that is not Saturday and Sunday represented in working-day calculations?
Is this value an instant or an interval, and if an interval, are its endpoints distinct?
Is the interval expressed as start and end or as start and duration, and are the endpoints inclusive or exclusive?
Is the duration an exact quantity or a nominal calendar description, and which units may it carry?
How is a nominal duration added across a zone transition or a short or long month?
Can an interval be unbounded at either end, and how is that represented distinctly from a missing value?
What granularity does this value actually assert, and is that recorded separately from its serialised form?
Is this a date-only or all-day value, and is it therefore zone-independent?
Which granularities and offset forms does this Dimension's adopted profile accept on input and emit on output?
How is a value that is known only approximately, or only to a bounded range, represented without inventing precision?
Is comparison between values of different granularity defined, and what does it return when they overlap?
Which binding does this field use, and where is that binding declared for machine consumption?
Which companion fields are mandatory for this binding — zone identifier, calendar key, granularity, resolved offset?
Is a floating value ever silently converted to an absolute instant on storage or transport?
When the value crosses a system boundary, which annotations travel with it and which are critical?
Which binding should be chosen for a newly modelled field, and on what test?
What frequency, interval and by-part filters define this rule, and in what order are they applied?
What anchors the expansion, and does the anchor itself belong to the generated set?
Is the rule bounded by a count or by an until value, and does the until value match the anchor's value type and binding?
For an unbounded rule, what expansion window is used and who sets it?
Which week start applies, and how does changing it alter the generated set?
When the underlying zone rules change, are previously expanded instances recomputed or frozen?
How is a single occurrence identified so that an override or cancellation can target it unambiguously?
Which dates are excluded and which are added outside the rule, and who authorised each?
Which calendar scale governs expansion, and is it declared explicitly rather than inherited?
What happens when a generated date does not exist in the target year — omit, move backward or move forward?
Do all consuming implementations expand this rule to the same set, and how was that verified?
Are overrides preserved when the base rule is edited, and how are orphaned overrides detected?
Which jurisdiction or sub-jurisdictional division does this holiday apply to, and do divisions within the same state differ?
Which authority proclaimed the holiday, and under what instrument?
Is the observed date the nominal date or a substitute, and what rule produced the substitution?
Does the holiday confer a non-working day, and for whom — all employers, public sector only, or specific sectors?
How far forward is the holiday calendar authoritatively published, and what is done beyond that horizon?
How are one-off, rescinded or retroactively declared holidays recorded without corrupting historical calculations?
Within which calendar system is this observance computed, and by which determination method?
Is the observance fixed in its own calendar, movable, or dependent on observation that cannot be predicted?
Which community or authority determines the date, and do communities in the same territory differ?
What evidence supports the date asserted for a specific year, and when was it confirmed?
Does the observance carry any civil effect, and where does that effect come from?
How does the system behave when a provisional date is later corrected?
Which weekend rule and which holiday sets compose this calendar, and over what period is it valid?
Which named centre or centres apply, and when several apply, is a date a working day only if it is one in all of them?
Which adjustment convention applies, and does it respect month boundaries?
How are day counts and deadlines computed — calendar days, working days, or working days with a cut-off time?
What happens to previously computed deadlines when a holiday is added or moved after the fact?
Which reference-data releases were used to build this calendar, so a past computation can be reproduced exactly?
Which release of each reference dataset is currently pinned, and where is the pin recorded?
Was the release signature or checksum verified before adoption, and by whom?
How is a change upstream detected, and how quickly must it be adopted?
Does any pinned dataset carry an expiry, and what is the behaviour after that instant?
Is versioning monolithic across all zones or independent per zone, and does the consumer handle both?
Can a historical computation be reproduced by re-pinning the releases it originally used?
What is the evidence class of this temporal fact — legal instrument, authority publication, mirrored consensus, or reconstruction?
Is the fact within a range the upstream maintainer declares unreliable, and is that warning propagated to consumers?
Where two authoritative sources disagree, which one governs here and on what documented basis?
When an upstream correction changes a historical value, what is done with results already published from the old value?
Who is accountable for the accuracy of each class of temporal fact in this Dimension?
Is the provenance chain from legal instrument to mirrored dataset to local record complete and traversable?

grok_only.name: What is the authoritative name and, if any, IRI of this time scale, and which master system assigns it?
What epoch origin does this scale use, in RFC 3339 if expressible, and is that origin an instant on another scale?
Is this scale atomic, Earth-rotation, POSIX/Unix civil, GNSS-derived, or a named realisation such as UTC(NIST)?
What integer or continuous offset relates this scale to TAI or UTC, and as of which observation time?
Has IERS Bulletin C announced a leap second at a given month-end, and is it positive, negative or none?
How is the leap second encoded in timestamps and iCalendar DATE-TIME values, and what does a non-supporting consumer do with second 60?
What maximum UT1-UTC difference and implementation deadline currently apply, and has the 28th CGPM yet adopted a successor resolution?
For a leap-second record, what is the event instant on UTC and what is the ingestion or observation time of the bulletin?
What is the current IANA tzid, and which obsolete names or links still resolve to it?
Which representative location and, if tabulated, ISO country codes and coordinates describe this timezone, and is it a location zone or a fixed-offset zone?
Which political bodies currently determine this zone's offset and DST rules, and which TZ Coordinator release recorded that consensus?
What CLDR or other locale-dependent labels should an agent show instead of the tzid, and is the zone Etc/Unknown?
At what instant does this transition occur, in which clock (wall, standard or UTC), and what are offset-before and offset-after?
Is this transition recurring DST, a one-off wartime or political offset change, a base-offset change, or a rename with no clock change?
Does this transition create a nonexistent local-time gap or an ambiguous fold, and how should an agent resolve a civil time that falls in it?
Is the operating ruleset a pinned VTIMEZONE snapshot or a named IANA zone interpreted with a stated tzdb version?
Which tzdb version, publication instant and signature verified the rules used for a conversion?
Is a proposed zone change still on the mailing list, in a release candidate, published, or later corrected?
Under what terms may a product redistribute tzdb, and must signatures and public-domain notices be preserved?
Does a requested historical conversion fall after 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, in recorded pre-1970 transitions, or in backzone/guesswork?
What CLDR BCP 47 calendar type, iCalendar CALSCALE/RSCALE token, or other master identifier names this calendar?
Is the calendar solar, lunar, lunisolar, imperial-era overlay, ISO-week overlay, or tabular versus sighting?
Which jurisdictions or communities use this calendar for civil law, religious law, or display only?
Which fields (era, year, month, week, day, day-period) does this calendar require, and which inherit Gregorian names from CLDR?
What is the era name, its calendar, its epoch date on a stated scale, and whether it is still open-ended?
What leap-day or leap-month rule applies, and who is authorised to declare an intercalation that is not purely algorithmic?
When did a jurisdiction adopt, skip or repeat civil dates, and in which calendars must both the old and new labels be stored?
Does this context use ISO week-date (WKST Monday, week 1 containing the first Thursday), iCalendar WKST, or a locale first-day-of-week?
Is this value an instant, a calendar date, a floating local time, a timezone-qualified civil time, or a duration, and on which TRS?
What are the beginning and end, are they inclusive, and which Allen relation holds against another interval?
Does the timestamp carry an RFC 9557 suffix naming an IANA timezone or other tags, and is that suffix consistent with the numeric offset?
What is the stated precision, and is the local offset unknown (-00:00) versus UTC-preferred (Z or +00:00)?
What is the FREQ, INTERVAL, UNTIL or COUNT, BY* parts and WKST of this rule, and what DTSTART anchors it?
Which additional RDATE instants and EXDATE exceptions apply, and are they DATE or DATE-TIME of a single type?
Over what query window should occurrences be materialised, and is the rule bounded or forever?
In which timezone and tzdb version are wall-clock recurrences expanded, especially across DST gaps and folds?
Which RSCALE calendar is used, and does it match a CLDR type such as hebrew, chinese or islamic-umalqura?
How is each non-Gregorian occurrence projected to a Gregorian DATE for civil systems that only store Gregorian?
If a consumer does not implement RFC 7529, what fallback (materialised RDATE list, skip, or error) is required?
What happens when a BYMONTH or named month is absent in a given lunisolar year?
What official name, jurisdiction, local identifier if any, and first-observed year identify this holiday?
Is this holiday a statutory day off for the general public, for public servants only, a bank holiday, or a commemorative day that is still a working day?
Is the date fixed, an nth weekday, computed from an observance, or a one-off proclamation, and which recurrence rule generates it?
Has this holiday been proclaimed, amended, substituted, or rescinded, and where is the instrument published?
Which days of the week are non-working weekend days for this jurisdiction or population, and from when?
If a holiday falls on a weekend or other non-workday, is it observed on the preceding or following workday, or not moved?
Given a Gregorian date, timezone and population, is the civil day a working day, and what evidence supports that classification?
Is the holiday and weekend dataset complete for the requested year and sub-national unit, or is completeness unknown?
What name, tradition or community, and local identifier distinguish this observance from a public holiday of similar name?
In which calendar is the date computed, is it movable, and what algorithm or authority supplies the year-by-year date?
Which jurisdictions have formalised this observance as a public holiday, and with what day-off status?
Does this observance occupy a civil date, a sunset-to-sunset interval, or a multi-day season, and in which timezone is dusk evaluated?

requirements: Resolve every provider-only bundle, layer and finding against primary evidence.
Resolve the model boundary and entry kind before accepting structure.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Record every rejected and deferred node with a reason.
Do not publish while any critical conflict remains unresolved.
